Additional Stacked Bar Charts

Primary Energy

Historical source: IEA data - IEA covers every category over 1990-2023. Nuclear, hydro, wind and solar are only reported at the carrier level, hence the |Electricity variables; geothermal is split into an electricity and a heat variable which stack into a single segment. - The IEA reports nuclear as primary heat, the models as direct equivalent, so nuclear is scaled by 0.334 in both the bars and the total. - The IEA primary energy total also covers waste and heat, to match the total to the bars, the difference is added to “Other”.

Carbon Capture by Origin

Final Energy by Carrier

Historical source: IEA data - The IEA carriers add up exactly to the IEA final energy total, bunkers included, which matches the models “Final Energy” used here (checked again on the current historical.mif: agrees to 1e-4 for 2018-2023).

Final Energy per Sector

Historical source: IEA data - The IEA has FE = FE|Industry + FE|Transport + FE|Buildings, so non-energy is inside industry and bunkers inside transport. Industry comes from the IEA’s own FE|w/o Non-energy Use|Industry; bunkers I still subtract, to match the models “Final Energy (w/o bunkers)”. - The IEA has no agriculture or other-sector split.

Final Energy per Sector and Carrier

Historical source: IEA data - The IEA only splits industry, buildings and transport by carrier, so the historical bars stay empty in the agriculture and other-sector rows. - The IEA nests non-energy use inside industry, whereas the models report it as its own sector. The sector totals need no assumption - the IEA reports FE|w/o Non-energy Use|Industry directly - but the carrier split still does: the IEA series used here has no non-energy-use breakdown by carrier, so for simplicity I assumed it all feedstock liquids and moved it out of industry liquids. (The current mif does have FE|Non-energy Use|Industry|Liquids|Fossil, but only on the IEA WEO 2025 rows, not the IEA series used here.) Be aware that this causes only approximated comparisons on gas and liquids carrier levels at industry and non-energy use that I would avoid/fix before showing in any publication.

Secondary Energy | Electricity

Historical source: Ember, plus BP for oil - unlike the IEA, Ember reports the generation total. - Ember has no oil; BP does, on the same basis (the two agree to within 1% on nuclear, wind, solar and hydro), so oil comes from BP. Not from the IEA: its SE|Electricity rows in this mif are labelled EJ/yr but sum to ~127 EJ, about twice the EU’s entire primary energy, so they are unusable. - Geothermal and other generation are still missing (no usable source), so the historical stack sits slightly below its own total.

Capacity | Electricity

Historical source: Ember, plus IRENA for geothermal - PRIMES does not report electric capacity at all and LIMES only reports the total, so those two bars stay empty. - Storage power capacity (Capacity|Electricity|Storage|Power) is stacked on top. It is not part of the reported “Capacity|Electricity” total, so wherever a model reports it the bar stands above its own total diamond by exactly the storage segment. Ember reports no historical storage, so the historical bars have no storage segment. - Ember covers every category except geothermal (about 0.9 GW in the EU), which comes from IRENA. The two combine cleanly - Ember’s renewables capacity is IRENA data anyway, hydro, solar and wind match to four decimals. - No source reports a usable historical capacity total across 2018-2022, so the historical bars carry no total diamond. Eurostat stops at 2018; the IEA WEO 2025 gives 2023 but is scope-inconsistent against Ember (solar matches to 0.02% while hydro is +67% and coal +52%), so it is not used.
